description: Evaluation criteria for Dev10x:diag-friction skill (formerly Dev10x:skill-reinforcement)

eval_dimensions.name: Offending Command Identification (Step 1/2/3)
eval_dimensions.description: The offending command is correctly identified (from context, an explicit argument, or SKILLS.md fallback) and matched against the canonical command-skill map read fresh from disk, never recalled from training.

eval_dimensions.name: Step 6 Follow-Up Retry Gate
eval_dimensions.description: When the triggering command was rejected, the reinforcement must block on AskUserQuestion offering to retry via the recommended skill, cancel, or defer — never a plain-text 'Want me to invoke X?' — and must be skipped when the command was informational or already approved.

eval_dimensions.name: Step 3b/3d Permission-Friction Audit
eval_dimensions.description: The audit reads live settings files to surface an existing pre-approved alternative when one exists, and proposes only a narrow, generalized allow-rule (never Bash(*) or a destructive-verb wildcard) when none does.

eval_dimensions.name: Step 3a Effective-File Coverage and Backfill Gate
eval_dimensions.description: Before auditing rule shapes, the skill checks whether the effective settings file carries the shipped catalog, names a propagation gap as such rather than diagnosing the individual command, and blocks on AskUserQuestion before any backfill write.

evals.name: Direct command-skill map match (kubectl)
evals.description: Agent used kubectl, skill identifies k8s match
evals.input: Agent ran 'kubectl get pods -n staging', user invoked /Dev10x:diag-friction

assertions.signal: identifies_offending_command — Output contains the kubectl command that was detected
recommends_correct_skill — Output recommends Dev10x:k8s as the replacement skill
includes_reason — Output includes explanation of why the skill should be used

evals.name: No command-skill map match falls back to SKILLS.md scan
evals.description: Agent used a command with no direct skill mapping

assertions.signal: acknowledges_no_match — Output states no direct skill match was found
suggests_related_skills — Output lists potentially related skills from SKILLS.md

evals.name: User-supplied command argument is used verbatim
evals.description: User passes command as argument to the skill

assertions.signal: uses_provided_command — Output identifies 'git push' as the command without scanning conversation
recommends_git_skill — Output recommends Dev10x:git as the replacement

evals.name: Rejected command opens the Step 6 retry gate via AskUserQuestion
evals.description: After a rejected command, skill offers follow-up via AskUserQuestion (not plain text)
evals.input: Agent ran 'Monitor' for CI polling, user rejected it and invoked /Dev10x:diag-friction

assertions.signal: follow_up_uses_tool — AskUserQuestion is called with retry options after the reinforcement message
offers_invoke_recommended_skill — Options include invoking the recommended skill (e.g., Dev10x:gh-pr-monitor) as the Recommended choice
offers_cancel_option — Options include cancel/discard to avoid resuming the rejected workflow
no_plain_text_followup — Output does not use plain-text questions like 'Want me to invoke X?' for the follow-up prompt

evals.name: Audit surfaces an existing pre-approved alternative
evals.description: When a rejected command was packed with chaining/prefixes but the unchained form is pre-approved, the audit surfaces the simpler form and cites the allow-rule
evals.input: Agent ran 'git fetch origin && git checkout develop' which was rejected; .claude/settings.local.json contains Bash(git fetch:*) and Bash(git checkout:*) in permissions.allow

assertions.signal: reads_settings_files — Output references at least one of: .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/settings.json, or ~/.claude/settings.json as the source of pre-approved rules
surfaces_preapproved_alternative — Output recommends splitting the command into separate Bash calls and names the matching allow-rule(s) (e.g., Bash(git fetch:*))
identifies_chaining_as_friction_cause — Output explains that && / ; chaining (or env-var prefix / cd prefix) shifts the effective allow-rule prefix

evals.name: Audit proposes a narrow, generalized allow-rule when none fits
evals.description: When no allow-rule covers even the simplified command, the audit proposes a targeted (narrow) allow-rule addition rather than a broad one
evals.input: Agent ran a command whose simplified form still has no matching allow-rule in any settings file

assertions.signal: proposes_targeted_allow_rule — Output suggests a narrow Bash(<prefix>:*) snippet and names the settings file it should be added to (typically .claude/settings.local.json)
avoids_broad_or_destructive_rules — Proposed rule does not include Bash(*) or wildcards that span destructive verbs

evals.name: Informational invocation skips the Step 6 gate
evals.description: When invoked informationally (not after a rejection), no follow-up gate is fired
evals.input: User invoked '/Dev10x:diag-friction kubectl' to learn the recommended skill, no prior rejection

assertions.signal: skips_follow_up_gate — AskUserQuestion is not called — the reinforcement message is informational only

evals.name: Catalog rule missing from the effective file is named as a propagation gap
evals.description: The offending command's rule is in the shipped catalog and in global settings but absent from the worktree's settings.local.json
evals.input: Agent ran 'pre-commit run --files foo.py' in a worktree and was prompted; Bash(pre-commit run:*) is in the catalog and in ~/.claude/settings.json but not in the worktree file

assertions.signal: runs_catalog_gap — Output reports missing allow/deny counts from the catalog-gap check for the effective settings file
names_propagation_gap — Output states the rule is in the catalog but missing from the effective file, rather than proposing it as a new rule
AskUserQuestion is called to offer the backfill before any write

evals.name: Report-only choice performs no write
evals.description: A non-empty gap is reported and the user selects Report only
evals.input: Effective settings file lacks 137 catalog rules; user answers 'Report only' at the backfill gate

assertions.signal: no_write_on_report_only — No ensure-base or seed-worktree invocation follows the gate; the settings file is unchanged

evals.name: Settings files are read via Read or audit_analyze_permissions
evals.description: The coverage step must not shell out to rg/grep/cat against ~/.claude/settings*.json
evals.input: Skill runs Step 3a and needs the contents of ~/.claude/settings.json

assertions.signal: avoids_shell_settings_read — No Bash rg/grep/cat/jq call targets ~/.claude/settings.json; the Read tool or audit_analyze_permissions is used instead

should_trigger: User says 'use the skills' after rejecting a bash command
User rejects a kubectl command and wants skill guidance
User says 'there's a skill for that'
should_not_trigger: Agent is already using skills correctly
User is asking about how to create a new skill (use Dev10x:skill-create)
User wants to list available skills (use Dev10x:skill-index)
The CLI command has no skill or MCP equivalent
